chapter: A41 — Sepsis et choc septique de l’adulte (I-03-Infectiologie)
author: /root/sentinelle_medicale
scope: Lecture complète des deux HTML candidats et des27 observations P1 ; vérification primaire ciblée des corrections, pas certification exhaustive de tous les chiffres/concepts inchangés. A41_b/pop_pa/c/d/pop2/glossaire/justifications non édités.

evidence_change_points.title: Définition, seuil et fonctions SOFA
evidence_change_points.change_and_implication: Seuil prognostique opérationnel, variables et coupures consensuelles ; six fonctions et non six défaillances. Deux clés et fenêtre précisent la causalité de la réponse dérégulée et la hausse aiguë ≥2.

evidence_change_points.title: Calcul du cas clinique
evidence_change_points.change_and_implication: Glasgow14 et PAM58 sans vasopresseur valent chacun1 : total initial exactement2, puis total7 avec résultats complets ; aucun dépassement implicite du seuil au premier calcul.

evidence_change_points.title: Catégories et sous-codes du même chapitre
evidence_change_points.change_and_implication: A41 contient déjà plusieurs agents ; liste des sous-codes A41, exemple Ecoli A41.51/+R57.2 si choc. A48.3 distinct et code agent seulement suivant règles applicables, non imposé par cette notice.

evidence_change_points.title: Formulation clinique et introductions
evidence_change_points.change_and_implication: Retrait des annonces de fabrication/revue ; les tableaux répondent à une question clinique, en-tête limité aux références. NEWS2 appartient à l’auteur P2.

evidence_change_points.title: Synthèses utiles sans répétition
evidence_change_points.change_and_implication: Encadrés abrégés en implications cliniques ; chiffres et notions utiles conservés dans leurs paragraphes.

evidence_change_points.title: Dénominateur suisse transparent
evidence_change_points.change_and_implication: 6098/21001=29,0 % arrondi ; note conserve le29,3 % imprimé et ne devine pas son dénominateur.

evidence_change_points.title: Mortalité cumulative
evidence_change_points.change_and_implication: ≈30 % à un an chez≥65 comprend22,3 % hospitalier ; suivi des survivants Prescott2018 séparé de la cohorte suisse. Fenêtre et Pareto transmis à leurs propriétaires.

evidence_change_points.title: Remplissage et noradrénaline
evidence_change_points.change_and_implication: Remplissage corrige absolue et une part de relative ; noradrénaline augmente tonus artériolaire ET veineux, peut mobiliser volume/précharge. Relative insuffisance de vasopressine limitée à certains patients. Banque preuve complémentaire proposée au root.

evidence_change_points.title: Attribution d’une dysfonction
evidence_change_points.change_and_implication: Thrombopénie ne vaut pas à elle seule preuve de défaillance due à infection ; rechercher dilution, médicaments, autre cause. Confusion isolée aussi à interpréter dans le contexte.

evidence_change_points.title: Corticothérapie et risques
evidence_change_points.change_and_implication: Prednisone/âge ont pu atténuer fièvre. Couverture de stress pour risque surrénalien actuel/récent non écarté :100mg puis200mg/24h parentéraux si hospitalisation, selon doses déjà reçues ; pas toute ancienne prescription.

evidence_change_points.title: Populations d’études et dénominateur microbiologique
evidence_change_points.change_and_implication: BALANCE identifié comme bactériémies sélectionnées avec exclusions, non tout sepsis. SOAP30%Saur et14%MRSA partagent le dénominateur de cultures positives, pas14%des Saur.

evidence_change_points.title: Urgence anatomique et antibiotique
evidence_change_points.change_and_implication: Décompression du rein infecté obstrué urgente ;≤6h est repère conditionnel/très faible de contrôle source, jamais motif d’attente. Asplénie : cultures si pas de retard, antibiotique avant imagerie ; purpura extensif n’attend pas le prélèvement.

evidence_change_points.title: Grades, âge et lactate
evidence_change_points.change_and_implication: Dès65ans PAM initiale60–65 conditionnelle/faible ; presseur concurrent solutés possible au cas par cas si choc instable ; lactates répétés pour sepsis avec lactate élevé OU choc, conditionnel/faible. MDR/anaérobies/antifongiques séparés avec leurs grades/risques.

evidence_change_points.title: Prélèvements et rendement des cultures
evidence_change_points.change_and_implication: Au moins2paires aérobie/anaérobie, ponctions distinctes, fabricant et8–10mL/adulte selonCHUV. RendementsLee89,7/98,2% et effetABCheng31,4/19,4% avec limites. Suspicion cathéter : simultanés, volumes égaux, sites/heure, même organisme etDTP≥2h.

exact_card_evidence.statement_and_certainty:
For adults with possible, probable, or definite sepsis or septic shock, we “recommend” collecting blood cultures as soon as possible and ideally before the administration of antimicrobial therapy.
Certainty of evidence: Low

For adults with sepsis-induced hypotension, we “suggest” initial IV crystalloid fluid bolus resuscitation followed by vasopressor support if hypotension persists.
Certainty of evidence: Very low
exact_card_evidence.remarks:
Remarks
In patients with unstable septic shock, immediate concurrent administration of vasopressors together with IV crystalloid fluid may be warranted on a case-by-case basis. Presence of unstable shock should be determined by physical examination. Suggestive clinical features of unstable shock include severely reduced blood pressure, mottled skin, ashen appearance, cyanosis/decreased oxygen saturation, tachycardia, and altered mentation.

exact_card_evidence.statement_and_certainty:
For adults with septic shock 65 years old or older, we “suggest” an initial MAP range of 60-65 mm Hg over higher ranges.
Certainty of evidence: Low

For adults with sepsis or septic shock and a specific anatomical diagnosis or source of infection that requires source control, we “suggest” early source control over late source control, ideally within 6 hr of diagnosis of sepsis or septic shock requiring source control.
Certainty of evidence: Very low

For adults with sepsis or septic shock at high risk of infection with a specific MDR pathogen, we “suggest” using empirical antimicrobial therapy with coverage for this MDR pathogen.
Certainty of evidence: Very low
exact_card_evidence.remarks:
Remarks
Risk factors for MDR pathogens include colonization with the MDR pathogen of concern, previous infection with the MDR pathogen of concern, prolonged use of broad-spectrum antibiotics, and prolonged hospitalization in a unit with a high prevalence of the MDR pathogen of concern.

exact_card_evidence.statement_and_certainty:
For adults with sepsis or septic shock at low risk of infection with a specific MDR pathogen, we “suggest against” using empirical antimicrobial therapy with coverage for this MDR pathogen.
Certainty of evidence: Very low

For adults with sepsis or septic shock, we “suggest against” using empirical antifungal therapy.
Certainty of evidence: Low
exact_card_evidence.remarks:
Remarks
Empiric antifungal therapy should be considered on a case-by-case basis in selected patients with sepsis or septic shock and risk factors for fungal infection, including immunosuppression, prolonged use of antibiotics, prolonged hospitalization, and intra-abdominal sources of infection.

exact_card_evidence.statement_and_certainty:
For adults with sepsis or septic shock without risk factors for anaerobic infection, we “suggest” using an empiric antibiotic regimen without anaerobic coverage.
Certainty of evidence: Very low
exact_card_evidence.remarks:
Remarks
When coverage of potential MDR pathogens is required, agents with anaerobic activity (e.g., piperacillin–tazobactam or carbapenems) are appropriate when alternative agents lacking anaerobic coverage are insufficient.

exact_card_evidence.statement_and_certainty:
For adults with sepsis or septic shock with specific risk factors for anaerobic infection, we “suggest” using an empiric antibiotic regimen that includes anaerobic coverage.
Certainty of evidence: Very low
exact_card_evidence.remarks:
Remarks
Risk factors for anaerobic infection include intra-abdominal or deep-seated gynecological/obstetric source of infection, necrotizing soft-tissue infection, head and neck infection, and CNS abscesses or empyema.

exact_card_evidence.statement_and_certainty:
For adults with sepsis and elevated lactate or septic shock, we “suggest” using serial lactate measurements to guide resuscitation.
Certainty of evidence: Low
exact_card_evidence.remarks:
Remarks
Fluid administration should be individualized after initial fluid bolus and monitoring of lactate decrement, rather than continuing fluids until lactate normalization is achieved.

evidence_from_author_report.title: Vasopressin deficiency contributes to the vasodilation of septic shock.
evidence_from_author_report.abstract: The hypotension of septic shock is due to systemic vasodilation. On the basis of a clinical observation, we investigated the possibility that a deficiency in vasopressin contributes to the vasodilation of septic shock. In 19 patients with vasodilatory septic shock (systolic arterial pressure [SAP] of 92 +/- 2 mm Hg [mean +/- SE], cardiac output [CO] of 6.8 +/- 0.7 L/min) who were receiving catecholamines, plasma vasopressin averaged 3.1 +/- 1.0 pg/mL. In 12 patients with cardiogenic shock (SAP, 99 +/- 7 mm Hg; CO, 3.5 +/- 0.9 L/min) who were also receiving catecholamines, it averaged 22.7 +/- 2.2 pg/mL (P < .001). A constant infusion of exogenous vasopressin to 2 patients with septic shock resulted in the expected plasma concentration, indicating that catabolism of vasopressin is not increased in this condition. Although vasopressin is a weak pressor in normal subjects, its administration at 0.04 U/min to 10 patients with septic shock who were receiving catecholamines increased arterial pressure (systolic/diastolic) from 92/52 to 146/66 mm Hg (P < .001/P < .05) due to peripheral vasoconstriction (systemic vascular resistance increased from 644 to 1187 dyne.s/cm5; P < .001). Furthermore, in 6 patients with septic shock who were receiving vasopressin as the sole pressor, vasopressin withdrawal resulted in hypotension (SAP, 83 +/- 3 mm Hg), and vasopressin administration at 0.01 U/min, which resulted in a plasma concentration (approximately 30 pg/mL) expected for the level of hypotension, increased SAP from 83 to 115 mm Hg (P < .01). Vasopressin plasma levels are inappropriately low in vasodilatory shock, most likely because of impaired baroreflex-mediated secretion. The deficiency in vasopressin contributes to the hypotension of vasodilatory septic shock.
